items.title: NYAI raises $1.5 million from Prominent Family Offices to build India's AI-native legal infrastructure platform
items.summary: NYAI, India's first AI-native legal infrastructure platform, has raised $1.5 million (approximately ₹13 crore) in a seed round subscribed by a consortium of prominent Indian family offices, with participation from strategic angel investors. The proceeds will be directed towards three ends. The first is technology enablement: enlarging NYAI's proprietary corpus of Indian statutory, regulatory and judicial material, and hardening the intelligence layer that sits above it. The second is the further build-out of AI-native compliance ecosystems, including the expansion of the company's compliance module into a full obligation-management system that maps India's regulatory architecture into a single, continuously updated dashboard. The third is deeper penetration into enterprises, listed entities and law firms, with the deployment and assurance functions such institutions require. A market defined by exposure, not efficiency The global legal services industry exceeds USD 1 trillion in revenue, yet under three per cent of it is technology-enabled. India's share of that opportunity is among the largest, and structurally distinct. Indian enterprises operate against a lattice of central, state and municipal legislation, delegated rulemaking, sectoral regulators and tribunals, each moving to its own cadence. The consequence is measurable. Indian companies collectively incur an estimated ₹95,000 crore each year in legal and regulatory penalties, while listed entities alone account for over ₹1.65 lakh crore in value erosion attributable to compliance failures, contract lapses and regulatory blind spots. The Digital Personal Data Protection regime is expected to add a compliance market of ₹10,000–12,000 crore annually. For the Indian enterprise, therefore, the principal return on legal technology is not the hour saved in drafting; it is the liability averted. "International legal AI platforms are engineered for Western legal systems, where the binding constraint is the cost of counsel," said Adv. Dr Chinmay Bhosale , Co-founder, NYAI. items.title: BCI has no business: Supreme Court bench led by CJI Surya Kant slams circular against NALSAR students
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday criticised the Bar Council of India's (BCI) now-withdrawn order that no law student of NALSAR Hyderabad's 2026 batch would be allowed to enrol as advocates on account of their campaign against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant . CJI Kant himself today slammed the BCI's move. "Naturally, this is absolutely uncalled for. It’s a dialogue between students and me. Who are they to raise an issue? This is totally uncalled for. In my student days I have been actively involved in student activities. Assuming even if they are wrong they have a right to protest. BCI doesn’t have any business," remarked CJI Kant. The CJI made the remark after Senior Advocate K Parameshwar mentioned the matter this morning before a Bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymlaya Bagchi and V Mohana. " BCI has no business of what’s going on in a university," submitted Parameshwar today before the Supreme Court. Even as it recorded that the BCI has since rescinded the action against the students and the inquiry into the protests, the Court proceeded to issue notice on the plea. It made in clear that no punitive action should be taken against NALSAR or any of its students or faculty or any other national law university by BCI. " Issue notice. Meanwhile no action shall be taken punitive action to be taken against student or faculty of any national law university/law university. BCI accepts notice. Pending circular has been withdrawn. Be that as it may let counter affidavit may be filed within 2 weeks. No punitive action to be taken against students of NALSAR in respect of the incidents mentioned in the subject letters," the order said. CJI Kant added, " Even in young days somebody makes a wrong statement that doesn’t mean they don’t have right to protest. Please tell all the students to get enrolled, join Supreme Court bar, we will empanel them for legal aid cases."

items.title: Litigant in Kerala attacks parents of lawyers who represented his wife
items.summary: Parents of two lawyer-siblings in Kerala were attacked by a litigant on Thursday night as retaliation for appearing against him in a case filed by his wife. According to a first information report lodged by the police, two men attacked the parents. The FIR was registered based on a complaint filed by the advocates' 79-year-old mother from the hospital where she was being treated after the attack. Her 80-year-old husband, the advocates' father, was stabbed repeatedly and he remains in critical condition. According to the FIR, the advocates represented the wife of one of the attackers who sought police protection from him due to domestic dispute. At around 5:30 pm on August 13, two men, including the irate litigant, forcefully entered the house of the advocate's parents and asked them where their son was. According to the FIR, the men were armed with knives and threatened to kill the advocates and their parents. When the advocates' mother asked them to leave, the attackers dragged the father out of the house, threw him on the ground, attempted to slit his throat and repeatedly stabbed him in the torso. Based on the mother's statement, Ernakulam Rural Police (Njarakkal) registered an FIR early this morning booking the two accused men under Sections 109(1) (attempt to murder), 118(1) (voluntarily causing hurt with dangerous weapons), 351(3) (aggravated criminal intimidation, 333 (house trespass after preparation for assault) and 3(5) (criminal act done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The Kerala High Court Advoactes' Association (KHCAA) has called an urgent General Body meeting to discuss the incident. The meeting will be held at 1:05 pm in the Association Hall today.

items.title: Brand protection in the era of social commerce
items.summary: The rapid growth of social commerce has fundamentally altered how businesses build brands, engage consumers, and generate revenue. Social media platforms are no longer limited to communication and entertainment. They have evolved into sophisticated commercial ecosystems where businesses promote products, interact with consumers, complete transactions, and cultivate long term customer relationships. Platforms offering live shopping, influencer collaborations, short video marketing, and integrated purchasing features have transformed the commercial landscape across India. This evolution has created significant opportunities for businesses of every size. Startups, established enterprises, and independent entrepreneurs now reach national and international audiences without maintaining extensive physical retail infrastructure. Brand visibility has become easier to achieve than at any previous time. However, increased visibility has also expanded the scope of trademark misuse, counterfeit activity, impersonation, deceptive advertising, and unauthorised commercial exploitation. Brand owners increasingly confront infringement occurring through influencer content, fake business profiles, copied product images, misleading advertisements, counterfeit listings, and fraudulent social media accounts. Indian trademark jurisprudence has progressively evolved to address these commercial realities. Courts have consistently recognised trademarks as valuable commercial assets deserving robust legal protection. Judicial interpretation now extends beyond conventional physical marketplaces and increasingly reflects the realities of digital commerce and evolving consumer behaviour. Social commerce functions differently. Mallya is accused of money laundering and siphoning off at least ₹3,500 crore out of the total ₹9,000 crore bank loans granted to his defunct Kingfisher Airlines. By it first circular, the BCI barred the entire 2026 batch from being enrolled as advocates for objecting to CJI Kant's participation as chief guest for the convocation of the 2026 batch. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that advocates acting as insolvency professionals are liable to collect Goods and Services Tax (GST) from recipients of their services and deposit it with the government under the forward charge mechanism [Kanwal Chaudhary v. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India]. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Shail Jain held that advocates providing insolvency and receivership services must obtain GST registration and comply with the requirements applicable to insolvency professionals as a class. “ An Advocate acting as an Insolvency Professional would, therefore, be governed by the ‘forward charge mechanism’, which is applicable to Insolvency Professionals, as a class, and not by the ‘reverse charge mechanism’, which is otherwise applicable to Advocates rendering legal services ,” the Court said. Justice Prathiba Singh and Justice Shail Jain Under the forward charge mechanism, the service provider adds GST to the invoice, collects it from the recipient and deposits it with the government. Under reverse charge, the recipient of the service is responsible for depositing GST. According to him, any GST payable on his professional fees had to be deposited by the corporate debtor under the reverse charge mechanism. items.title: Delimitation: CM Vijay writes to PM Modi, urges freeze on Lok Sabha seats at 543
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 13, urging the Union government to permanently freeze the Lok Sabha’s strength at 543 and retain the existing distribution of seats among states and Union Territories. In his letter, the Chief Minister pointed out the resolution adopted by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on August 12, which called for constitutional amendments to preserve the existing level of representation for states. “The existing number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to the states should be made permanent at the current level. Current distribution of seats among the states must be maintained. I kindly request you to consider the resolution passed by Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and bring necessary Constitutional amendments in this regard,” Vijay said in his letter. The Assembly resolution also sought the implementation of 33% reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha without changing the existing strength of 543. According to the resolution, the southern states could lose a significant number of parliamentary seats after population census if Article 81(2)(a) is applied. The Assembly cited the 1967 delimitation, when Tamil Nadu's Lok Sabha representation was reduced from 41 seats to 39. Vijay said any delimitation based on the post-1971 population that changes the existing strength of the states would cause “lasting injustice” to the southern states. He pointed out that these states had implemented population-control programmes and achieved economic growth while also carrying out healthcare and public welfare measures. The resolution was backed by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the TVK’s coalition partners, while the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), Desiya Murupokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK), and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) opposed it.

items.title: NALSAR VC does not agree to BCI inquiry, says will probe if its permissible
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. After the Bar Council of India (BCI) wrote to NALSAR University of Law’s Vice-Chancellor ordering an inquiry into why students opposed the invitation extended to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant to attend the university’s convocation, Vice-Chancellor Srikrishna Deva Rao said the university would assess whether such an inquiry was permissible. “We would have to assess whether such an inquiry was a constitutional exercise of their powers,” the VC said. “In order to assist the University, assess whether conducting such an inquiry would be constitutional and permissible under the University’s governance regulations, the matter will be placed before the Executive Council of the University,” Srikrishna said. He added that once the Executive Council’s consultation was completed, the university would communicate its decision to the BCI. The BCI on Thursday, August 13, wrote to NALSAR Vice-Chancellor Professor Srikrishna Deva Rao seeking an inquiry based on a report into what led students to protest against the invitation extended to CJI Surya Kant. “The vast majority of the students of NALSAR (2026 pass-out students) are innocent and were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect... It has further been reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating the innocent students,” BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra said in the second letter. Around 450 students at NALSAR had opposed the invitation to CJI Surya Kant to attend the university’s convocation, citing his remarks in July regarding police excesses during student protests. During protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, students were beaten by Delhi Police personnel. The CJI had declined to hear a petition concerning alleged police brutality against the protesting students, reportedly saying, “Don’t waste our time. We are not interested in videos, we don’t have time to watch.” The remarks prompted students from NALSAR’s 2026 graduating batch to oppose the CJI’s invitation to the university’s convocation. On Thursday, August 13, the BCI had initially directed state bar councils not to enrol any students from NALSAR’s 2026 graduating batch as advocates. It has further been reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating the innocent students,” BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra said in the second letter. Speaking to TNM, a student of the outgoing 2026 batch who was among those who signed the representation opposing the CJI’s visit said that the redacted statement from the BCI did little to assuage their fears. items.title: TVK govt signs MoUs worth Rs 67K crore, projects 1.06 lakh jobs
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Tamil Nadu government on Thursday, August 13, exchanged 104 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) at its first major investment conclave since the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) assumed office. The event included 97 company MoUs involving investments of Rs 67,452 crore and seven institutional pacts. These agreements are projected to create 1,06,998 jobs. The ‘Vettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave 2026’ was held in the presence of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay. The government said the latest commitments took the total investments attracted in its first 100 days to Rs 1.02 lakh crore. The closed-door event, from which members of the news media were excluded, saw the MoUs exchanged in the presence of the Chief Minister. Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce Minister S Keerthana said the government was seeking to position Tamil Nadu as a destination for domestic and foreign investment while expanding into higher-value industries. Data centres accounted for the largest share of the investments at Rs 26,417 crore, followed by automobiles at Rs 17,073 crore, renewable energy at Rs 15,787 crore and critical engineering at Rs 9,525 crore. Lighthouse Green Data Centre committed Rs 10,000 crore to establish a hyperscale data centre in Thoothukudi, making it the single largest investment announced at the event. Airtel’s data-centre subsidiary Nxtra committed Rs 1,417 crore. The investments were spread beyond Tamil Nadu’s established industrial hubs. According to the government, 54 projects worth Rs 40,722 crore, with 61,480 projected jobs, will be located outside the state’s four core industrial districts. Ramanathapuram is set to receive its first major industrial investment, with Phoenix Kothari Footwear Limited committing Rs 1,000 crore to a project expected to create 10,000 jobs. The project is also expected to create employment opportunities for women in the district. Kancheepuram received the highest number of projects, with 20, followed by Chennai with 14, Tiruvallur with 13 and Thoothukudi with 10. The Hinduja Group, which has been operating for 111 years, committed Rs 2,500 crore across renewable energy, electric mobility, automotive, financial services, energy, battery-charging infrastructure and digital mobility solutions. items.title: Karnataka Govt vs RSS: Cabinet clears Bill requiring permission for use of public property
items.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved a Bill requiring organisations to obtain government permission before holding activities on public property. The Bill, approved on Thursday, August 13, comes amid a prolonged dispute between the Congress government and the RSS over the latter's use of public spaces. The Karnataka Regulation of Use of Government Premises and Public Property Bill, 2026, is expected to be introduced during the ongoing monsoon session of the legislature. The Bill has been drafted by the Home Department headed by Priyank Kharge. The proposed legislation will replace an October 18, 2025 government order that required private organisations, associations and groups to obtain prior permission to use government premises or public property. The order applied to private associations, societies, trusts, clubs and other bodies, whether registered or not, but was stayed by the Karnataka High Court on grounds including violation of fundamental rights. The earlier order had required organisations to seek permission at least three days before an event. The proposed Bill is expected to establish a statutory framework for granting permission to use government lands, buildings, playgrounds, parks, roads and other public assets, besides providing for penalties in cases of misuse or damage. While the government has said the legislation will apply to all organisations, it comes against the backdrop of repeated disagreements between the Congress government and the RSS over the use of public property for its meetings and route marches. Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said the Bill was not aimed at any particular organisation and that prior permission would be required for anyone seeking to hold an event on public property. “We’re saying prior permission will be required for any programme, whoever it may be. In Bengaluru or anywhere else, permission is needed,” Shivakumar said. He added that organisations could not use public spaces without following due process. “There needs to be proper documentation for events. Be it you or me, we cannot barge on to the streets according to our whims and fancies,” he said. Home Minister Priyank Kharge also rejected suggestions that the Bill was specifically aimed at the RSS.
